items.summary: Parameter Labs describes an exploit against ChatGPT's artifacts pattern, formerly called Canvas and now HTML previews. The vulnerability lets untrusted code in a sandboxed iframe inject custom HTML via innerHTML, bypassing CSP rules through YouTube oEmbed to execute JavaScript. This enables fetching private user data from APIs and exfiltrating it via image references. A malicious share URL could let another signed-in user access their data or take actions on their behalf. OpenAI closed the hole and paid a $5,000 bug bounty.
items.title: Parameter Labs Exploits ChatGPT Account Takeover Vulnerability

items.summary: Samsung launched its ultra-premium W27 foldable phone, based on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, with sales beginning November 13 exclusively in China. Prices start at 18,999 yuan (about ₹2.72 lakh), and the top-end 1TB model costs 21,999 yuan (around ₹3.15 lakh). The device features a 200MP camera, dual displays up to 120Hz, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, 16GB RAM, and direct satellite connectivity. There is no announced India launch.
items.title: Samsung W27 Foldable Launches in China at ₹3.15 Lakh

items.summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar called for reducing political interference in energy markets and diversifying global supply chains, saying disruptions were placing a disproportionate burden on developing countries. Speaking at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, he urged the grouping to work toward de-politicising markets and preventing production concentration in a few geographies.
items.title: Jaishankar Urges De-Politicisation of Energy Markets at G20

items.summary: Two nationalist leaders, Serbia's Aleksandar Vučić and Hungary's Viktor Orbán, lost power within a year of each other after popular movements won their elections. Both were defeated by youth-driven campaigns that used AI tools to coordinate tens of thousands of election monitors who blocked intimidation at polling stations. The Student List took 140 seats in the 250-seat Serbian parliament, matching the number Tisza party had held earlier in Hungary's smaller parliament. Few expected either leader to concede peacefully; Vučić admitted defeat at 21:30 on Sunday evening, and Orbán declined to comment when contacted by the BBC. Both men may now face prosecution for corruption as similar special prosecutors investigate them.
items.title: Serbian and Hungarian Leaders Fall After Youth-Led Elections

items.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, Democratic nominee for Michigan's US Senate race, asked congresswoman Haley Stevens to stay away from his campaign events after their planned joint appearance fell through. Citing distractions and party unity ahead of the tight contest against Mike Rogers, El-Sayed said he did not want the race derailed by disputes over a political ad. The rift has drawn concern among Democrats who view the election as essential.
items.title: Michigan Senate candidate El-Sayed asks ally Stevens to skip events

items.summary: A federal judge in Miami dismissed President Donald Trump's multibillion-dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch with prejudice, ruling he failed to prove actual malice. The suit concerned a 2003 album containing a letter bearing his name for Jeffrey Epstein's birthday. Judge Darrin Gayles called the case grasping at straws as it sought to manufacture flaws in the reporting.
items.title: Federal Judge Dismisses Trump's Lawsuit Over Epstein Letter Story

items.summary: Chipotle will open its first Singapore restaurant on Level 2 of Jewel Changi Airport, unit #02-200. The American chain offers a customisable menu of burritos, bowls, tacos, quesadillas and salads. Operations in Singapore and South Korea are handled by S&C Restaurants Holdings, a joint venture between Chipotle and Sangmidang Holdings, which also runs Shake Shack and Paris Baguette there. Hee Soo Hur called the launch an exciting entry into Singapore’s food culture.
items.title: Chipotle Announces Singapore Debut at Jewel Changi in 2027

items.summary: Saul Canelo Alvarez reclaimed the world super-middleweight title on Saturday with a unanimous decision, defeating Christian Mbilli inside a 25-square-meter ring. The judges scored it 115-112, 116-111 and 117-10. Alvarez said he still loves boxing after his first loss came from Terence Crawford in September 2025.
items.title: Canelo Alvarez regains super-middleweight title in Riyadh comeback win over Mbilli

items.summary: South Korea's exports rose 93.7 per cent to $115.28 billion in October from a year earlier, the trade data showed on Sunday, beating market expectations and marking the sharpest jump since January 1974. Semiconductor sales jumped 259.4 per cent as prices and volume stayed high amid continued investment by global big tech firms pursuing artificial intelligence leadership, while computer sales surged 496.6 per cent.
items.title: South Korea Reports Sharp October Export Surge, Strongest in Over Half a Century

items.summary: RIL’s September quarter presentation said the private refiner raised its market share in Africa and Europe by about 50%, tapping Australia, Kenya, Tanzania and Mediterranean markets. Its oil-to-chemicals business drove fiscal second-quarter earnings with a 68% surge in Ebitda to a record Rs 25,203 crore, as O2C revenue grew 44% to Rs 231,601 crore amid high energy prices and West Asia conflict lifting crude oil prices by 41%. The company cited geopolitical disruptions tightening global refining margins. RIL expects tight product supplies near term.
items.title: Reliance Expands Fuel Exports, Posts Record O2C Ebitda in September Quarter

items.summary: American filmmaker Zarina Zabrisky, who has reported in Ukrainian-controlled Kherson for three years, spoke to France 24's Gavin Lee about the events of the past 24 hours. The exchange draws on testimonies from Oleshky.
items.title: Filmmaker Shares Oleshky Testimonies With France 24 Reporter

items.summary: The Vietnamese government announced on Saturday that it will lower its average retail electricity price by 2 per cent and eliminate the special consumption tax on gasoline from November 1. The measures aim to support economic stability, social welfare, and business activity amid a growth target above 10 per cent this year.
items.title: Vietnam Cuts Electricity Prices and Gasoline Tax From November

items.summary: An altercation on February 7, 2025, in the Ukhrul district village of Litan is cited as a trigger for renewed ethnic clashes between Nagas and Kukis. A torchlit confrontation turned into a beating after three Kuki men confronted a drunk friend; accounts diverge sharply over who began it, with Naga and Kuki witnesses giving opposite versions of what followed. The night's violence spread across hill districts in late February, adding 65 lives to the state's ethnic death toll, which has reached at least 363 over three years. Police say tribal disputes are settled by custom rather than reported, while community representatives describe decades-old land tensions as the deeper cause.
items.title: A drunken brawl in Litan ignites Naga-Kuki violence across Manipur

items.summary: Simon Willison announced on 31st October 2026 a small user experience improvement to the datasette-llm plugin, which now automatically picks up LLM's default model. Users can run Datasette Agent without explicitly configuring a default model via uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db, removing the previous need to specify gpt-6-astra with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model. He noted larger Datasette Agent upgrades are still in development and linked several recent articles dated 28th October through 9th October 2026.
items.title: Simon Willison ships datasette-llm plugin update

items.summary: Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah is expected to make his first bilateral foreign visit, planned for late November around the 22nd. Persons aware of the matter said preparations are underway, with foreign secretary Vikram Misri set to travel to Kathmandu on November 4 and India's ambassador-designate Sudhakar Dalela arriving early next week. The Rastriya Swatantra Party government is calling for a reset in bilateral ties, focusing on trade, connectivity and border security. Foreign minister Shisir Khanal said the partnership should move away from past friction toward development diplomacy. Shah has avoided foreign trips since becoming PM in March. Details of agenda items remain unconfirmed by officials.
items.title: Nepal's Rapper PM Likely to Make First Foreign Trip to India

items.summary: The TechCrunch Founder Summit, presented by Fidelity Private Shares, is set for November 4 at Boston's SoWa Power Station. It offers founders and VCs structured networking through a Braindate-powered lounge with scheduled conversations, roundtables, breakout sessions, an Expo Hall, and closing reception, plus all-week Side Events in Boston. With four days until doors open, organizers urge early registration to save up to $100 on a pass and receive a second pass free.
items.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit Promotes Intentional Networking With Early Pass Savings

items.summary: Chevron is raising its exploration budget this year by 50% compared with last year, McLachlan told the Financial Times in an interview in September. The company says spending could top $1. 5 billion, up from just below $1 billion in 2025. Kevin McLachlan leads Chevron’s revived upstream program and took over the exploration arm last year after joining from France’s TotalEnergies. Two years ago Chevron drilled about 10 exploration wells per year; its 2027 plan includes drilling 20 exploration wells, possibly up to six appraisal wells. About half of the budget is now going into undeveloped frontier basins in South America, Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean, up from around 20% a few years ago. Chevron also raised acreage by 35% over the past year and has announced discoveries in Nigeria and Angola. Analysts at Wood Mackenzie said the Middle East conflict highlighted concentration risk in unstable regions.
items.title: Chevron Boosts Exploration Spending by Half

items.summary: Unalaska, an Alaskan port closer to Asia than Washington DC, is under strain as high diesel prices squeeze its seafood industry while federal funding disruptions hit local institutions. Fisherman Oystein Lone faced rising fuel costs ahead of the Bering Sea crab season and said his community 'is at the bottom.' The town's public library lost a book grant from the Institute of Museum and Library Services, the Museum of the Aleutians had its National Endowment for the Humanities funding canceled before being restored after a lawsuit, and KUCB radio station lost half its budget when Congress cut public media money. Unalaska's power cost rose to as much as $0.36 per kilowatt hour from $0.22 last year. Residents say Trump-era policies have damaged the town, though some federal programs like a rural health initiative may bring relief.
items.title: Diesel Prices and Federal Cuts Strain Alaska's Unalaska

items.summary: Adrian Massey, a former food developer made redundant in 2010, worried most about his mortgage. He and wife Tulay cleared their debt early — £30,000 saved — buying their six-bedroom Banbury home for £280,000 before he lost his job. Their monthly payment was about £1,400 at 6.1%. They set up a standing order to overpay £500 a month, added pay rises and lump sums of up to £2,000, then remortgaged in 2013 to a 2.5% tracker with no overpayment limits. By 2021 they were mortgage-free seven years ahead of schedule, using freed cash for their business ATM Food Innovations. Moneycomms notes small overpayments can save thousands; expert David Hollingworth warns early repayment charges may erode benefits and a savings buffer is advisable.
items.title: Couple Becomes Mortgage-Free Seven Years Early Through Overpayments

items.summary: Factory released Droid 1. 0, its largest update to the model-independent coding agent harness, making programmatic tool calling (PTC) on by default for ten models including GPT-6. 1 Sol and Kimi K3. Under PTC's Script mode, one model request can drive hundreds of tool calls while only printed output returns to the model; Factory reports a unit-test fix that took 41. 6 s instead of 56. 8 s using two requests and about 61,000 tokens versus roughly 36 requests and 3. 1M tokens directly. In its own October 23–28, 2026 runs on Terminal-Bench 4, Droid scored 65. 2% with Claude Opus 5. 5 at $4. 73 per passed task (self-reported), the highest of every harness tested; it also cut cost by up to 24% and took less time than direct tool calling.
items.title: Factory Ships Droid 1.0 With Programmatic Tool Calling as Default

items.summary: Delhi is preparing for the INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting up to 10 lakh attendees. Delhi Police anticipates around 50,000 people and has deployed more than 4,000 personnel plus 200 CCTV cameras. The event includes a 'Chalo Dilli' march from Minto Road-Connaught Place junction at noon, followed by the rally from 10am to 5pm.
items.title: Delhi Prepares for INDIA Bloc Anti-CEC Rally at Ramlila Maidan

items.summary: Tens of thousands are expected in Delhi for a mega opposition rally seeking the chief election commissioner's resignation and electoral reforms, with leaders claiming up to a million could attend. The Congress-led INDIA alliance and pressure group Cockroach Janta Party have pledged support. Protests stem from criticism of a voter-list revision that removed 130 million names from draft rolls across India. Delhi police permit the rally but require it end by 5pm, with CCTV cameras installed and no marches outside the site. Both the BJP and Election Commission deny allegations of vote theft; The Indian Express reported in September that commissioner Gyanesh Kumar made key decisions unilaterally. Rahul Gandhi called the march 'just the trailer,' saying Sunday's rally would be several times bigger.
items.title: Delhi opposition rally seeks election commissioner's resignation amid voter-list row

items.summary: Six longevity researchers say popular anti-ageing claims are often unscientific or harmful, and they name the myths people should stop repeating. A 2026 report by XRC Brand Capital Fund found that longevity-inspired web searches were four times as high in late 2025 as a year earlier. Dr Sofiya Milman of Albert Einstein College of Medicine says much circulating advice is not science-based, and she lists six myths: research aims to extend healthy life span rather than length alone; US life expectancy rose only about six months from 2009 to 2019 while healthy years declined; no drug or supplement has been shown to extend human life span; women live longer but often with more illness; weight loss is not always protective, especially for adults over 65; and reaching 100 depends heavily on genetics. Steven Austad, Aladdin Shadyab, Pankaj Kapahi and Viviana Perez Montes back these points.
items.title: Longevity Experts Warn Against Six Common Anti-Ageing Myths

items.summary: Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk vowed on Saturday night to complete a contested overhaul of the constitutional court, which has been paralysed for over a decade amid disputes between Law and Justice (PiS) and the EU. Government-backed judges seized procedural control Friday, suspending PiS-appointed leaders and triggering protests that drew riot police. The European Commission urged president Karol Nawrocki to approve parliament-nominated judges. Experts remain divided on whether the government's move is lawful.
items.title: Tusk Defends Constitutional Court Overhaul Amid Protests

items.summary: The Trump administration reportedly plans to deport more than 150 Afghan immigrants back to Afghanistan through Pakistan, media reported Friday. Advocacy groups warn the move could endanger their lives. The plan follows last year's travel bans and efforts to end special immigrant visa protections for Afghans after the August 2021 Taliban takeover.
items.title: U.S. administration plans deportation of Afghan immigrants via Pakistan

items.summary: Julius Dam is marking its fiftieth year since construction following a drought in Mount Isa, where the city once ran short despite Lake Moondarra. Its concrete multiple-arch and buttress design lets excess water overtop without harm, according to University of Queensland professor Alexander Scheuermann. Operator Sunwater says it remains Queensland's only dam of its kind and can hold 107,500 megalitres. A seven-person team in Cloncurry maintains the structure and pipelines; ongoing maintenance will be essential as rainfall patterns change.
items.title: Julius Dam marks half-century of supplying outback water

items.summary: Western Australian rapper Kurrungaya Bieundurry, known as Kayps, chose a photograph of his late grandfather — who helped organise the 1979 Noonkanbah protest against an oil company drilling at a sacred site — to cover his debut album Bunuba Baby. The album reached number 2 on the Australian hip hop charts within a week of its August release and has been nominated for triple j's unearthed artist of the year, with Bunuba Baby up for Australian album of the year at the J Awards. Kayps said the protest galvanised the Kimberley land rights movement and hopes younger people reconnect with their culture.
items.title: WA rapper credits grandfather's land rights photo for debut album

items.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is reportedly preparing guidelines to invest up to 3 per cent of its fresh annual inflows in alternative investment funds (AIFs), according to media reports published on October 29 and 30, 2026. The proposal would follow a September communication from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade regarding participation in the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, and is expected before EPFO’s Central Board of Trustees in November. Officials note it does not mean 3% of the entire corpus will move into AIFs immediately, as safeguards are being considered. Shrikant Goyal described the step as reflecting growing confidence in the asset class.
items.title: EPFO Considers Allocating Up To 3% Of Fresh Inflows To Alternative Investment Funds

items.summary: Glenn Phillips is set to face India in the fifth and final bilateral T20I at Seddon Park, Hamilton on Sunday (November 1). He has scored 276 runs in the ongoing series. To break Phil Salt's all-time record of 331 runs from December 2023 against the West Indies, he needs another 56 runs. Phillips also requires just 15 runs to surpass Mark Chapman's New Zealand record of 290 runs from 2024.
items.title: Phillips poised for T20I series runs record against India

items.summary: Fergus Farrell, an Irish man who suffered a spinal cord injury in 2018 after a gym accident, is walking approximately 3,000 miles across the United States. Doctors reportedly gave him only a 5% chance of regaining mobility before his recovery. The journey runs from the Brooklyn Bridge in New York to Santa Monica Pier in California over roughly 75 consecutive days and covers about 4,500 kilometres. As reported by Connacht Rugby, the walk aims to raise funds for Spinal Injuries Ireland while highlighting rehabilitation and determination. Farrell frames it as a personal statement on recovery rather than an endurance feat alone.
items.title: Irish Man Undertakes Cross-Country Walk After Spinal Injury

items.summary: Actress Divya Dutta discusses her recurring collaborations with actor Manoj Bajpayee, whom co-star Sudhir Mishra cast against each other in the film Gajab Raat. She recounts his comment calling her a chor (thief) as a scene-stealer and expresses affection for him, praising his generosity, humility and effortless screen presence. Dutta notes their four prior films—Veer-Zaara, Special 26, LOC and Traffic—but clarifies they had never shared the frame until now. She reflects on playing complex women across Irada (2017), Dhaakad (2022) and Chiraiya (2026), resisting narrow labels and asserting her desire to play varied roles without being boxed in.
items.title: Divya Dutta on Repeated On-Screen Rivalries With Manoj Bajpayee

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters took to French streets Saturday in a third consecutive weekend over living costs and education, France's government estimating 320,000 nationwide — fewer than the Oct. 17 (500,000) and Oct. 24 (410,000) rallies but still significant. Authorities reported about 300 arrests so far, down from 800 a week earlier, while organizers cite higher numbers. Youth-led marches also occurred in Germany's Gen Z regelt rally across more than 30 cities and in Lisbon; The Hague saw little protest after police frisking. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of very high disorder risk after dark on Halloween as clashes erupted near Porte de Charenton with tear gas used to disperse crowds.
items.title: French Youth Protests Sweep Europe on Living Costs and Education

items.summary: After Australia were bowled out for 111 all on day five at Newlands, needing 288 to win, they lost the third Test and levelled the series 2-1. Former opener David Warner led a savage reaction against what he called disgraceful batting, while Mark Waugh also condemned it. Australian media urged introspection ahead of December-January home Tests versus New Zealand.
items.title: Australia's cricket team faces backlash after South Africa series win in Cape Town

items.summary: China's Communist Party concluded its fifth plenum, expelling 33 senior members amid Xi Jinping's widening anti-corruption campaign. The meeting ran Monday to Thursday; of the 376 central committee members named in 2022, only 279 attended – more than a quarter absent. Joseph Torigian and Neil Thomas say it signals preparation for next year's party congress and Xi may seek a fourth term. Since coming to power in late 2012, the campaign has punished 7.9 million individuals, including over 960 senior officials, per Zhang Fuhai. Analysts warn stricter discipline could stifle local experimentation.
items.title: Beijing Plenum Expels Officials as Xi Prepares for Next Congress

items.summary: Hundreds of thousands took part in a third consecutive weekend of largely peaceful demonstrations across France against soaring living costs and inequality, with an estimated 320,000 rallying nationally including 70,000 in Paris. Clashes nonetheless erupted as masked demonstrators hurled paving stones at police; the interior ministry said several hundred rioters attacked security forces, some using a Molotov cocktail that injured one officer. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it an “attempted murder” and blamed far-left groups, while far-right leader Marine Le Pen demanded severe punishment for those responsible. Youth organisations put turnout at nearly half a million nationally including 200,000 in the capital. A night-time curfew was imposed in central Paris neighbourhoods on Saturday and Sunday.
items.title: French Protesters Clash With Police Over Cost of Living

items.summary: In Indore, Madhya Pradesh, two finance company branch managers were killed when a speeding crane rammed their motorcycle near Navda Panth Bridge under Chandan Nagar police station limits on Friday night around 9 pm. Rohit Meena died at the scene; Naushad later succumbed to his injuries after being rushed by colleagues and passers-by. The driver fled, prompting an ongoing police probe.
items.title: Two Finance Company Branch Managers Killed in Indore Road Accident

items.summary: The Health and Medical Education Department of Madhya Pradesh is rolling out a paperless system across all government hospitals from November 1, 2026. The initiative covers medical college-affiliated hospitals and sub-health centres, sending OPD slips to patients via SMS or digitally. GMC Dean Dr Kavita Singh said the hospital has run it as a pilot for six months.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh Launches Paperless Government Hospitals From November 2026

items.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saturday that Ankara put forward practical proposals to address global crises and strengthen international cooperation during a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, US. Speaking on the sidelines of the two-day gathering hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Fidan described this year's meeting as particularly timely given growing energy disruptions and mounting pressure on supply chains. He said Türkiye seeks meaningful contributions focused on problem-solving rather than simply taking a different position from other countries. Fidan also credited President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's leadership for strengthening the country's international standing.
items.title: Türkiye Frames Problem-Solving Diplomacy at G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting

items.summary: On Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan urged Russia and Ukraine to reach a peace agreement, warning the nearly five-year war risks further regional escalation. Speaking in Atlanta at a G20 foreign ministers' meeting, he said such wars are no longer sustainable. He stressed that Europe must also reconcile with Russia for lasting settlement, cited economic strain from the Strait of Hormuz closure, and called for restoring Black Sea grain trade.
items.title: Turkish Foreign Minister Urges Russia and Ukraine Peace Deal, Warns of War Spread

items.summary: A youth initiative called Gen Z regelt held a demonstration at Berlin's Brandenburg Gate on Saturday, with police reporting around 5,000 participants while organisers claimed some 11,000. Protesters demanded more education funding and an end to rearmament. The rally drew pro-Palestine activists, including representatives of the monitored newspaper Junge Welt and radical left groups such as Linksjugend solid and Revolutionäre Linke. Berlin police said there was no reliable evidence of extremist control over the group but warned that some extremist actors were mobilising for possible escalation. Organisers distanced themselves from a separate planned protest at Rosenthaler Platz, which authorities say is being promoted in far-left circles and where hundreds more participants are expected.
items.title: Berlin student rally draws large crowds amid extremist mobilisation fears

items.summary: Across Europe, governments are weighing measures to hold rioters, their families and social media platforms accountable for protest-related damage. France has led the debate: its Senate approved a proposal by 229 votes to 105 letting authorities recover compensation from family benefits after unrest costing more than €1 billion ($1.1 billion). The law would make people who knowingly join or stay in violent crowds liable up to €10,000 for others' damage. Human rights groups warn it could punish those not personally involved and harm poor families. Amnesty International France's Nathalie Godard cautioned over seizing benefits. The bill still faces the National Assembly, where no bloc holds a majority. AP reported all details; insurance payouts during 2023 riots reached €793 million across 16,400 claims per France Assureurs.
items.title: European Governments Explore Recovering Costs of Riot Damage From Families and Social Media

items.summary: At Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations in Gujarat, PM Modi addressed the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and warned against “dimagi Naxals. ” He called the Opposition an ‘Avrodh Paksh’ rather than a Virodh Paksh, saying it obstructs development. Modi said India’s unity is its strength amid global conflict and fuel shortages. Referring to a World Bank report, he stated 50 crore Indians were lifted out of poverty in the 10-12 years leading up to 2024, with severe-poverty rates falling from 27 out of 100 people to less than three out of 100. He inaugurated 23 development projects worth Rs 307. 83 crore and laid foundation stones for eight more worth Rs 118. 88 crore, bringing the total outlay across 31 projects to Rs 426. 71 crore.
items.title: Modi Condemns Opposition as Obstruction at Unity Day Rally

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), met Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee in Delhi on Saturday. He thanked her for supporting the outfit's youth-led protests and standing with members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka during their arrest by Delhi Police. Although the CJP expressed solidarity with Sunday's INDIA bloc rally against alleged 'vote chori', Dipke clarified that the party would not formally join, citing its independent and politically neutral identity. Banerjee praised the activists as movement pioneers and invited them to West Bengal.
items.title: CJP Founder Rejects INDIA Bloc Rally Despite Meeting Banerjee

items.summary: The INDIA bloc held a symbolic mock parliament and public impeachment proceeding against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging he orchestrated the deletion of over 13 crore voters during the Special Intensive Revision process. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge leveled six charges, while Rahul Gandhi called for his trial for treason. BJP rebutted the claims as a 'parliament of theatrics,' defending its revision formula covering absent, shifted, deceased and duplicate electors.
items.title: INDIA Bloc Stages Mock Impeachment of Election Chief Amid Voter Deletion Dispute

items.summary: The Finnish National Gallery opened "Arcana Borealis – Northern Women and Esotericism" at Ateneum Art Museum, its first large-scale show examining how women artists from the Nordic region and Sápmi engaged with esotericism. It brings together more than 200 works by 50 artists until 28 February 2027. Co-curator Marja Lahelma noted art history has long focused on male genius, while Nina Kokkinen highlighted blurred boundaries between fine art and craft.
items.title: Finnish National Gallery Opens Esotericism Exhibition

items.summary: Ramachandra Guha reflects on Vallabhbhai Patel through Rajmohan Gandhi's biography, first published in 1991 and now reissued after 35 years. He notes the book's rich research into Patel's life and its emphasis that Nehru and Patel argued often yet reconciled repeatedly, ending every dispute with unity. Guha frames this reading against a changed political climate since Narendra Modi became prime minister in 2014, when Patel has been elevated while Nehru was criticised. Quoting Gandhi's preface to the new edition, he observes that exaggerating their rivalry serves as a distraction and urges readers to see the strength of the three men coming together after every crisis.
items.title: Guha reviews Gandhi's biography of Patel amid renewed political focus

items.summary: An eighth-month pregnant Trinamool Congress supporter in West Bengal's Cooch Behar delivered a stillborn baby two days after being assaulted allegedly by Bharatiya Janata Party workers on Wednesday, The Telegraph reported. Her husband Debajit Barman said she intervened to save him and was also beaten before the couple was hospitalized; he registered a complaint against 10 persons while police arrested only two alleged BJP associates. BJP leaders denied any party link, blaming an unrelated local dispute.
items.title: Pregnant TMC Supporter Assaulted in Cooch Behar, Delivers Stillborn Baby

items.summary: On October 24, Lara Croft marked the 30th anniversary of the first Tomb Raider (1996), which critics credit with letting women lead in video games. The character reportedly has sold 100 million copies and appeared on 2,300 magazine covers across roughly 30 countries toured by its creator. Paula Sáez Pérez, author of La última exploradora, notes the franchise moved Lara from a sexualized object toward iconic status; Miguel Aguerralde adds she helped end questions about women in games today. The reboot trilogy began in 2013 with writer Rhianna Pratchett, and upcoming titles include Legacy of Atlantis next year and Catalyst scheduled for 2028.
items.title: Lara Croft Marks Three Decades as Tomb Raider Franchise Looks Ahead

items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the INDIA bloc in a symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at his residence in New Delhi. The Opposition alleged that Kumar facilitated deleting 13.2 crore voters, altered Form 6 without approval, and acted under instructions from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. These remain allegations made by the Opposition and have not been established as findings against the CEC. Kharge said the campaign aimed to protect the Election Commission's credibility rather than target Kumar personally.
items.title: Congress leader Kharge accuses Election Commissioner of vote theft on Modi's orders

items.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah announced his marriage to journalist Nidhi Razdan on Saturday, sharing wedding photographs on social media. The couple wed after his July 2025 divorce from Payal Nath, whom he married in 1994 with two sons. Their divorce followed years of legal battles over cruelty allegations and a monthly maintenance order of Rs 1.5 lakh to Payal and Rs 60,000 each for their sons.
items.title: Omar Abdullah Marries Journalist Nidhi Razdan

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met Ghana's John Dramani Mahama for bilateral talks a day after the Moscow Russia-Africa summit. Ghanaian media reported that Accra has begun discussions with Rosatom to build its first nuclear power station, while Mahama said at the summit Ghana is pursuing a diversified energy mix to secure its grid.
items.title: Ghana Opens Talks With Russia on Its First Nuclear Power Plant

items.summary: Vercel Labs has released agent-desktop, an open-source CLI and C library that lets coding agents drive native desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux by reading the OS accessibility tree instead of screenshots. Version 1.0.2 shipped October 30, 2026 under Apache-2.0. The tool embeds no LLM or GUI; each command prints one JSON envelope with refs for every actionable element. Vercel reports skeleton snapshots cut tokens by 78% to 96% on dense Electron apps like Slack, VS Code and Notion, though it offers no independent benchmark yet. Ref actions are headless, retry-safe and fail closed rather than guessing at the UI.
items.title: Vercel Labs Releases agent-desktop for AI Agent Computer Use

items.summary: On Madhya Pradesh Day, Aashish Chandorkar, Counsellor at India's Permanent Mission to the World Trade Organization in Geneva since September 2021, reframes Vidisha as a hidden jewel of Indian temple architecture. Though historically linked to Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Shivraj Singh Chouhan politically, the region—situated where the Betwa and Bes rivers meet—is far more significant spiritually. Its temples document nearly a millennium of evolution from rock-cut shrines to stone craftsmanship across Sunga, Gupta, Pratihara and Paramara patronage. Sites include the Udayagiri caves under Chandragupta II, the Heliodorus Pillar dating around 113 BCE, and the Bijamandal conceived on a scale rivalling Khajuraho in the 11th century. While Khajuraho receives attention, districts like Vidisha have not attracted devotees or history enthusiasts in significant numbers. As Madhya Pradesh turns 70 this year, Chandorkar calls for a micro-tourism vision and credible plan to realise it as potential economic activity complementary to the state's industrial growth.
items.title: Madhya Pradesh's Untapped Temple Heritage on Its 70th Anniversary

items.summary: Chinese tech giant Alibaba Group announced a partnership with Apple on Saturday, integrating its Qwen AI model into Apple Intelligence. The feature will be available for testing in the latest iOS developer beta starting November 4 and roll out to Chinese users via the official iOS 27.3 release in December, according to Alibaba. Users can choose whether to enable it and what information to share; Alibaba said user requests or responses won't train its model.
items.title: Alibaba Partners With Apple to Integrate Qwen Into Apple Intelligence

items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States is examining a report that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy plot. The New York Times reported that intelligence officials concluded a Singapore-linked figure funneled information to Beijing after interacting with Huang. China dismissed the claims as groundless speculation, while Trump expressed support for Huang and confirmed he would investigate further.
items.title: Trump Says US Is Closely Reviewing China Spy Allegations Against Nvidia CEO

items.summary: Political analyst Sanjay Jha alleges government pressure behind the leadership dispute at Tata Sons, citing regulatory delays over Suraj Sanghi Finance and Tata Sons deregistration, a stalled Maharashtra Charity Commissioner probe into Tata trusts filed in May 2026, ₹44,000 crore semiconductor subsidies before the 2024 elections, and electoral bonds from the Tata Progressive Trust totaling around ₹800 crore — nearly 85% of its donations. Jha argues a casting vote overrode the majority owner’s 66% holding in board decisions. The article frames these as allegations requiring investigation rather than established facts.
items.title: Analyst Alleges Government Pressure Behind Tata Boardroom Battle

items.summary: Uppal police and the Central Crime Station Uppal team arrested a 25-year-old woman, identified as Paga Jaya, for alleged involvement in a series of house burglaries. Police recovered gold and silver ornaments, cash, and an iPhone 17 worth approximately Rs 70 lakh. The case began after resident Gangam Bhaskar Reddy reported his locked home broken into on October 27; police suspect her role in five cases across Uppal, Medipally, Bhadradri Kothagudem II and Jagathgirigutta stations.
items.title: Woman arrested over Hyderabad house burglaries after wearing burqa

items.summary: A newsletter opens with how the weekend was invented, from Saint Monday in 19th-century Britain to Henry Ford's five-day, 40-hour workweek introduced in 1926. It then turns to Apple's iPhone Duo, which shipped in 2026 as one of John Ternus' first launches after he became CEO. Within hours of sale, some units developed bright lines and cracks across their inner displays, with a few users reporting problems after just a handful of folds and hearing crunching noises when opening the device. Apple acknowledged the issue and offered replacements but has not explained its cause; one theory is that a support bar inside the hinge isn't retracting properly, putting pressure on the flexible display.
items.title: iPhone Duo Cracks Prompt Late-Foldable-Phone Questions

items.summary: US Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley wrote a letter to Google CEO Sundar Pichai with 9 questions about the company’s push of A.I. products into schools, following an investigation into how its tools affect schoolchildren. They claimed test scores have declined and set November 2 as the deadline for a response, citing Wall Street Journal reporting that interviewed more than 60 teachers, parents, students and clinicians.
items.title: Senators Demand Answers From Google Over Classroom AI Push

items.summary: Business Today compares two premium smartphones in India: the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max and the iPhone 18 Pro Max. The article highlights that OPPO offers three 200MP rear cameras with a Hasselblad partnership, an 8,000mAh battery supporting 80W wired charging, while Apple emphasises camera processing, video features and its software ecosystem. On price, the OPPO starts at Rs 1,99,999 for the 512GB variant, whereas the iPhone begins at Rs 1,79,900 for 256GB but reaches up to Rs 3,29,900 for its largest model. The piece notes that camera megapixels and battery capacity are different measurements, so real-world testing is needed before a verdict.
items.title: OPPO and Apple Flagships Compared on Cameras, Battery and Price

items.summary: A survey of young Indian adults explores how Gen Z celebrates Diwali, blending traditional rituals like puja, diyas and rangoli with new habits such as curated outfits, branded gifts, social media photos and parties. Respondents describe balancing family values with self-expression, noting that online glamour creates pressure to attend events, spend money and keep up appearances while some avoid firecrackers for environmental or safety reasons.
items.title: Young Indians Rethink Diwali Through Personal Expression and Social Media

items.summary:
South Korea’s exports rose 76.1% year-on-year in working-day-adjusted terms for October, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources reported on Nov 1, with unadjusted growth at 93.7%. Semiconductors led gains, jumping 259% to US$56.4 billion. The strength bolsters cases for Bank of Korea rate hikes in November ahead of data due Nov 3 and a decision on Nov 26, as the economy expands unevenly amid strong chip demand and elevated inflation. Governor Shin Hyun-song said exports could push annual shipments past US$1 trillion for the first time in 2026.

Bloomberg
items.title: South Korea’s chip-driven exports surge in October, fueling rate-hike bets

items.summary: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government released on Oct. 29 a report by the Independent Committee reviewing last November's Tai Po fire, which killed 168 people. Based on 30 hearings and more than a million documents, the report details failures behind the disaster. The response centers on accountability and reform, covering political responsibility, criminal liability and administrative accountability, alongside reforms to prevent similar tragedies.
items.title: Hong Kong government responds to Tai Po fire with accountability and reform package

items.summary: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said the India-US trade agreement is 'at the finish line for a very long time,' expressing confidence both sides would close it. He cited India's nearly two decades to finalize its pact with the EU as context.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Near Finish Line, Says Sergio Gor

items.summary: As the Canton Fair marks its 70th anniversary, more than 30,000 exhibitors and around 340,000 overseas buyers are expected to attend. The fair has witnessed rapid upgrading of China's trade scale over the years. CGTN reporter Zheng Songwu walked the exhibition halls since the 140th edition opened on October 15th while investigating why international buyers keep returning.
items.title: Canton Fair at 70 draws returning global buyers

items.summary: The INDIA bloc held a symbolic public impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Mallikarjun Kharge's residence, with Congress media head Pawan Khera noting the chair Meira Kumar used had belonged to Jawaharlal Nehru. The opposition accused him of allegedly deleting voters' names and demanded his removal. BJP called it a mockery of Parliament.
items.title: Congress Highlights Nehru Chair Used in Symbolic Impeachment of Election Commissioner

items.summary: At a Chalo Dilli rally held at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on Sunday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urged participants to support local traders by shopping from their stores during the festive season. The appeal followed objections from trader associations concerned that the November 1 gathering could disrupt business in key commercial markets.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Urges INDIA Bloc Rally Attendees to Support Delhi Traders

items.summary: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) issued a travel advisory for Nov 6 to Nov 9, warning that heavy traffic is expected at the Woodlands and Tuas land checkpoints during the Deepavali long weekend. ICA encouraged travellers to plan ahead and use non-peak hours, noting it has stepped up security checks since Feb 28 amid heightened global tensions. During recent school holidays from Sep 4 to Sep 14, more than 6. 1 million travellers crossed both checkpoints, peaking at more than 599,000 on Sep 4 - surpassing the previous record of more than 598,000 crossings on Jun 19, 2026.
items.title: ICA Warns of Congestion at Singapore-Malaysia Checkpoints Over Deepavali Weekend

items.summary: Binance, described as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said it would resume withdrawals in phases after recovering about 95% of $6.3 billion stolen from its platform in what the FBI has tied to North Korea and called the world's largest digital heist. The first phase was set for Sunday between 0600 and 0900 GMT and included bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens. Binance said the remaining 5% of less liquid assets may take longer to source.
items.title: Binance Restarts Withdrawals After Recovering Most Stolen Funds

items.summary: State Bank of India’s economic research department (ERD) says the country’s 10-year Government Security yield could settle in a range of 6.75 per cent - 7 per cent by March-end 2027, citing a US spread and historical analysis. Group Chief Economic Adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh adds that yields topped 7.15 per cent-7.2 per cent recently but warns a short-term flare-up to 7.6 per cent is not ruled out. The ERD also notes roughly ₹1.52 lakh crore of G-Sec excess supply, partly offset by bond switches and buybacks cutting the borrowing requirement by ₹1.23 lakh crore. Published November 1, 2026.
items.title: SBI Ecowrap Forecasts India’s 10-Year G-Sec Yield by March-End 2027

items.summary: India's primary market is cooling after a record-breaking October, with Vedant Poly Fabs set to be the only new company opening its initial public offering next week. The slowdown follows Jio Platforms' Rs 30,188 crore debut on October 28, which listed at a premium of 21.36% and drew bids worth Rs 4.9 lakh crore. Meanwhile, six companies with open issues are scheduled to list during the coming week, bringing total expected listings to 13, including five mainboard firms, subject to final exchange schedules.
items.title: Indian IPO Market Slows After Record Jio Listing

items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on Friday that Russian teams may compete at next year's men's and women's ice hockey world championships, overturning International Ice Hockey Federation decisions to exclude them. CAS upheld appeals from the Russian Ice Hockey Federation against IIHF bars during the 2026-27 season, finding insufficient evidence of security concerns warranting continued exclusion.
items.title: CAS Clears Russian Teams for Ice Hockey World Championships in 2026-27 Season

items.summary: Binance announced it would resume withdrawals in phases after covering 95% of the $6.3 billion stolen from its platform, described as the world's largest digital heist and tied by the FBI to North Korea. The remaining 5%, Binance posted on X late Saturday, involves less liquid assets that may take longer to source. Withdrawals would begin between 0600 and 0900 GMT Sunday across bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and other tokens.
items.title: Binance Restarts Withdrawals After Recovering Most Stolen Funds

items.summary: Indian Railways launched a new overnight Vande Bharat Sleeper service connecting SMVT Bengaluru and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai, departing at 12.15 pm (quantity-208-216) under train number 27652 (quantity-280-285). The route includes eight stops across Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra. Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel HD Kumaraswamy and Minister of State for Railways V Somanna are expected to attend the inauguration on its launch day. This service adds to Indian Railways' expanding overnight sleeper network, which first introduced services on the Howrah-Guwahati corridor in January 2026 (date-2094-2098).
items.title: Indian Railways launches Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper train

items.summary: The European Commission said on Saturday it is closely monitoring the crisis surrounding Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, following a live-broadcast confrontation outside the court building on Friday night. A spokesperson told Euronews that appointing eight new members lies within the Sejm’s constitutional power and urged Polish authorities to keep the tribunal functioning per its constitution and EU case law. Prime Minister Donald Tusk condemned Friday’s events as “scandalous incidents” while vowing independent justice, amid accusations of a coup from opposition parties and condemnation from European Conservatives and Reformists co-chair Nicola Procaccini over what she called a grave violation of the rule of law.
items.title: EU Commission Defends Polish Parliament’s Power to Appoint Constitutional Court Judges

items.summary: A new Council of Europe report warns that economic losses from coastal erosion exceed €1 billion per year across 28 European countries and could reach €800 billion annually by century’s end. Co-author Fanis Spanos calls coastlines among Europe’s most valuable assets, while Anthony Buchanan says traditional sea walls are becoming unsustainable as sea levels rise toward another 44 cm by 2100.
items.title: Council of Europe Report Urges Coastal Relocation

items.summary: The Gold Coast Suns won their final home-and-away game, defeating Greater Western Sydney by 9.8 (62) to 7.11 (53), but finished just 0.2 percentage points behind Carlton for fourth place. The loss of the double chance meant they could not replace Carlton in the finals. Charlie Rowbottom said post-game: 'Obviously we're happy to get away with the four points, but I wanted to finish fourth.' She added: 'We'll take the long way home.'
items.title: Gold Coast miss finals berth despite Giants win

items.summary: State-owned oil marketing companies raised the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder by ₹10 to ₹2,820 from Sunday, ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, per PTI. This is the second straight monthly increase after hikes on October 1 and September 1. Aviation turbine fuel rose by ₹1.37/litre to ₹138.50/litre in its fourth consecutive rise. Domestic LPG at ₹942 for a 14.2-kg cylinder was unchanged.
items.title: Indian OMCs raise commercial LPG and jet fuel prices before festivals

items.summary: Karnataka is celebrating its 70th Kannada Rajyotsava on Sunday, November 1. The Bengaluru police imposed traffic restrictions around Sree Kanteerava Stadium that day. According to reports, more than 20,000 schoolchildren are expected to arrive in 300 to 400 buses, so the police announced route changes and parking prohibitions on several roads near the stadium.
items.title: Bengaluru police set traffic and parking rules for Kannada Rajyotsava

items.summary: Bryan Caplan argues that large language models are poor Bayesians, claiming they either move toward the speaker or fail to update when shown counterevidence. In response, ChatGPT concedes this is a genuine failure mode but notes there is no theorem requiring equal updating in both directions; under calibration assumptions, weaker-than-expected arguments should still trigger negative updates even if valid.
items.title: Caplan and ChatGPT Debate Whether LLMs Update Like Bayesians

items.summary: North Korea said Sunday it tested cluster-bomb warheads for tactical ballistic missiles a day earlier, its Korean Central News Agency reported. Defense officials quoted the agency saying the Standard Type 2 warhead could turn into ashes an area of 12 to 13 hectares at peak power.
items.title: North Korea Tests Cluster-Bomb Warheads on Tactical Missiles

items.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced about 90% of the roughly $6.3bn stolen in a record hack, with withdrawals set to resume on Sunday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said users will not bear the financial impact and that around $6.34bn of company funds is being used, drawing partly from its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users. The FBI says North Korea-backed TraderTraitor actors were behind the theft on or about October 29, 2026; Binance said it had already set aside those funds to cover losses as Bitcoin and Ethereum fell after the news.
items.title: Binance Covers Most of $6.3bn Hack Losses as FBI Blames North Korea

items.summary: Justice Thomas Bradley has been sworn in as Queensland's 28th governor at the state parliament, replacing Dr Jeanette Young. He previously served on the Supreme Court from 2018 and moved to the Court of Appeal in 2025. In his first address he said he aims to spend time across Brisbane and communities statewide. Premier David Crisafulli called it a significant moment for Queensland.
items.title: Queensland Swears In Justice Thomas Bradley as 28th Governor

items.summary: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late Saturday as clashes erupted with police across German cities, following largely peaceful cost-of-living protests. Violence spread to Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg after protesters targeted emergency workers. Organisers Gen Z regelt said demonstrations aimed for peace; spokesperson Lina Friedrich called them a fight against war. Authorities reported up to 18,000 protesters in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin.
items.title: German Cost of Living Protests Turn Violent in Frankfurt

items.summary: Supporters and cadres from across India gathered at Ramlila Maidan for a mega rally organised by the opposition INDIA bloc, with participation from Congress, CPI and allied trade unions. The mobilisation centres on allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision process and demands that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign. Opposition leaders addressed the crowd to counter accusations of anarchy while BJP mounted its own demonstration amid tightened security.
items.title: Opposition INDIA bloc rally draws crowds in Delhi

items.summary: Bao Shujun, a researcher at China's National Development and Reform Commission, explains the rationale behind the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China's fifth plenary session, held in Beijing from October 26 to 29, 2026. The article reflects his views rather than CGTN's official position. He argues that full and rigorous Party self-governance underpins high-quality economic development by curbing corruption, ensuring policy continuity, and improving the business environment as China transitions between its 14th Five-Year Plan close and 15th Five-Year Plan start. The plenary session adopted a resolution on party self-governance and proposed mechanisms to prevent officials from engaging in corruption while strengthening accountability systems for economic governance decisions.
items.title: China's Party Pledges Integrity Drive for Economic Growth

items.summary: A car crashed into a parked Municipal Corporation tractor-trolley on a flyover near Police Lines in Jalandhar, Punjab, killing two friends returning home from a birthday party. The victims were singer Yo Yo Honey Singh's nephew Vidit Olak and Aarav Talwar, son of the owner of Pappy Sweets. Baradari police station SHO Sahil Chaudhary said sanitation workers had parked the tractor-trolley to collect garbage around 3 am when the Volkswagen struck it.
items.title: Two Friends Killed When Car Strikes Parked Tractor on Jalandhar Flyover

items.summary: Neocloud firms, which lease computing warehouses to developers like Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta, are at the centre of a debate over their financial soundness. Gartner analysts predict 80% will cease independent operations by 2030, while Forrester expects several acquisitions amid shaky finances. CoreWeave carries $35.1bn (£26.3bn) in debt and its stock fell about a quarter last month; peers like Nebius shed similar amounts. Founders often trace to crypto mining, and the sector now depends on hyperscaler spending plans that recently disappointed investors. Some firms describe market reactions as irrational, while others warn of consolidation among smaller players.
items.title: Obscure AI Data Centre Firms Draw Investor and Analyst Concern

items.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who took charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on Saturday, outlined his priorities under a vision he called ‘VAYU’ at an address in New Delhi. He said it stands for Vigilance and Readiness, Aatmanirbharta through indigenous aircraft like the Tejas Mk1A, II and AMCA, Yukti via AI-enabled systems, and Unity of effort with other armed forces. Dixit added that drones, precision weapons, space, cyber, AI and the electromagnetic spectrum are reshaping warfare.
items.title: New IAF chief Dixit unveils VAYU vision for modernising air force

items.summary: The SUMP Affected Area Youth Association (SAAYA) called on November 2 for a shutdown across Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts of Arunachal Pradesh to protest arrests of agitators opposing the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. In an emergency meeting held October 29, SAAYA unanimously resolved the call in coordination with other community groups. The movement opposes forced surveys and deployment of central armed police without consent, citing fears over submergence of ancestral villages and loss of land. The state government maintains the exercise is only a preliminary feasibility assessment requiring environmental clearances before construction.
items.title: SAAYA Calls for Three-District Shutdown Over SUMP Project Arrests

items.summary: Three men from the Kuki community were killed Saturday in a fresh exchange of gunfire between unidentified armed groups in Noney district, Manipur, according to a police official. Two more Kuki civilians found dead shortly after. Clashes since February have claimed 68 lives; overall violence since May 2023 has killed at least 306 persons and left about 60,000 displaced. The Kuki Inpi Manipur blamed the state for failing to provide security.
items.title: Three Kuki Men Killed in Manipur Gunfight

items.summary: After the Calcutta High Court ordered social media platforms to remove Friendship Files: How Modi and Adani Stole India, Scroll points readers toward the underlying reporting. The court passed a pre-trial injunction without hearing the other side after Gautam Adani's firm filed a Rs 50-crore defamation suit against Sabeer Bhatia and others; Bhatia later clarified he only circulated it. Scroll instead suggests reading five reports covering Adani's early ties to Modi, cheap land for Mundra port, his coal empire traced to 2015 auctions, the Mumbai airport acquisition following a June 2020 CBI case against GVK Group, and project growth ahead of elections.
items.title: Scroll offers reports behind Adani documentary takedown order

items.summary: The FBI said Saturday that North Korea was behind a theft of more than $6 billion (€5. 36 billion) in virtual assets from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026. In a statement it named TraderTraitor as the responsible actors and urged exchanges to block related transactions. Binance said it is using company funds worth over $6. 34 billion to buy back roughly 90% of the stolen assets, with the remaining 10% less liquid tokens that may take longer to replenish.
items.title: FBI Blames North Korea for Record Binance Crypto Heist

items.summary: Six Indian tourists lost contact while trekking toward Shey-Phoksundo Lake, the deepest in Nepal, after heavy snowfall hit Numla and Bagla Pass areas. Nepali officials say they remain out of touch; a Nepal Army team joined search efforts. Dolpa Chief District Officer Junu Hamal said the group ignored local warnings about dangerous mountain conditions. Separately, 244 tourists reached Upper Dolpa, including 51 foreign nationals from outside SAARC regions.
items.title: Six Indian Trekkers Vanish on Nepal Lake Expedition

items.summary: Police in Bengaluru said a group allegedly smeared ink on playwright Addanda Cariappa during a theatrical performance, accusing him of portraying Mahatma Gandhi as anti-national. The incident occurred Saturday at a film academy in Banashankari. A complainant group and the playwright filed separate complaints; one complaint was lodged by Kushal Hanumegowda and 14 others alleging the play 'Gandhi Hatheya Kicchu' depicted Godse as a hero. No FIR has been registered yet, though investigation continues.
items.title: Bengaluru Police Probe Ink-Smearing of Playwright Over Gandhi Portrayal

items.summary: This Morning Briefing dated Nov. 1, 2026 rounds up several news items. It reports that G20 foreign ministers concluded two days of discussions in Atlanta on energy security, supply chains and geopolitical tensions, per a US presidency statement; French protests drew about 15,000 people across 65 actions with police using tear gas in Lyon and Grenoble; the Yemeni army captured the Huwayshian mountain range east of Al-Hazm after battles with Houthis. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he agreed with Erdogan to establish a new Black Sea grain corridor, per Anadolu. The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7; Gabby Williams led with 30 points and scored 28 in the second half. US rapper Macklemore performed at London's OVO Arena Wembley to close his Free Palestine Tour, featuring Greta Thunberg. Dutch professor Jan Rotmans is developing an AI version of himself, expected online by end of 2026 per NOS.
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers G20, Protests and WNBA Final

items.summary: A research report by Emkay Global Financial Services says a renewed Iran conflict after the November 3 elections could push oil prices higher, pressuring India's balance of payments and equities. It contends crude is unlikely to fall post-midterms, noting Democrats may win both chambers with about 60 per cent probability but that tariffs stay largely unaffected due to Trump's executive authority.
items.title: Emkay Report Warns US Midterms Won't Ease India's Oil Risks

items.summary: In Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, civil and military authorities have joined forces to revive Beirchha Lake and the Gambhir River. Following grassroots efforts by the Janapav Gram Panchayat, the Indian Army's Station Headquarters constituted a multi-agency Board of Officers (BOO) headed by an Army War College Colonel. The board will survey defence land, prepare maps and register plans, identify infrastructure for relocation and document trees over 15.24 cm girth. It must submit findings by November 30, 2026. Janpad Panchayat CEO Giriraj Dubey said the joint team would improve groundwater recharge, drinking water security and green cover.
items.title: Army and Civil Administration Form Board to Revive Beirchha Lake and Gambhir River

items.summary: Delhi and the National Capital Region will enforce stricter winter pollution restrictions from November 1 until January 31, 2027. Non-BS-VI vehicles registered outside Delhi cannot enter the capital, affecting around 10 lakh older petrol and diesel vehicles, while electric, CNG and emergency vehicles are exempted. Construction dust bans continue, offices require only 50% physical attendance with staggered timings, parking fees double at public facilities except DMRC ones, and a No PUC rule applies at roughly 500 pumps fitted with ANPR cameras. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta appealed for compliance.
items.title: Delhi-NCR Enforces Winter Pollution Rules From November

items.summary: Almost 140 people were arrested at the largest mass demonstration under Andy Burnham’s premiership opposing the proscription of Palestine Action, outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London. The Metropolitan police said: “139 people have now been arrested,” with officers continuing to make arrests. Defend Our Juries, which organised the event, estimated around 400 gathered and cited more than 4,000 arrests for supporting Palestine Action since the ban took effect. Protesters described the gathering as a stand against what they called genocide in Gaza. The protests precede an appeal at the UK supreme court on 4 November challenging Palestine Action’s designation as a terror group.
items.title: Nearly 140 Arrested at London Protest Against Palestine Action Ban

items.summary: Delhi will deploy nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel plus around 250 AI-enabled CCTV cameras at the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1. Organisers project up to 10 lakh attendees; Delhi Police arranged for 50,000 based on venue capacity. The event targets Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and electoral roll revisions amid Opposition allegations of deleting 13.2 crore voters.
items.title: Delhi Prepares Security and Traffic Plan for INDIA Bloc Rally

items.summary: Crypto exchange Binance said on Saturday it has replenished 90 per cent of the assets stolen in a record $6.3 billion hack, using company funds to buy new tokens and commit to covering the remaining 10 per cent so users would not bear financial impact, co-CEO Richard Teng stated. The FBI blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor unit for converting stolen assets into ethereum. Binance set aside around $6.34 billion from its Secure Asset Fund for Users and other reserves, and plans to reopen withdrawals on Sunday after taking a new proof-of-reserves snapshot as of 0000 GMT October 31.
items.title: Binance Replaces Most of $6.3 Billion Hack Losses

items.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saturday that Ankara put forward practical proposals during a G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio as preparation for the December leaders' summit in Miami. Speaking to Anadolu and TRT on 31 October 2026, Fidan described this year's gathering as timely amid growing global crises, including energy disruptions and supply chain pressure. He said Türkiye prioritizes constructive problem-solving over simply differing from other countries, presenting substantive proposals aimed at resolving current issues and preventing future ones. He also held bilateral meetings with representatives from more than half of the participating countries.
items.title: Türkiye Frames Problem-Solving Role at G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting

items.summary: Wes Streeting says he began stockpiling food and water weeks ago in case of a national emergency, telling the Times that household resilience is spreading as people budget for paydays. He said his department has ramped up spending while warning that 'spending more money badly is not virtuous.' Chancellor John Healey wants defence funding at 3% of GDP by 2030 and 3.5% by 2035, after asking departments to find 1% cuts for investment.
items.title: Defence Secretary Says He Stockpiled Supplies Amid Rising Threats

items.summary: The Trump administration is considering a program that would pay parents up to $9,000 annually to stay home with children, using reallocated federal funds previously supporting single mothers and low-income families. The proposal reportedly came from JD Vance. Erica Hall of Seattle described the financial strain dual-income parenting creates amid rising childcare costs. Experts warn the plan favors one family structure while ignoring working parents' needs; Chandra Childers said draining resources could raise rates for other families, and Liz Hipple noted stronger support would come from wage or paid-leave policies instead.
items.title: White House Considers $9,000 Annual Payment for Stay-At-Home Parents

items.summary: The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA bloc) organised a large-scale protest at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on 1 November, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Security arrangements included nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, with Delhi Police planning for a crowd of 50,000. Opposition leaders cited electoral irregularities during the Special Intensive Revision as justification.
items.title: INDIA Bloc Deploys Thousands for Delhi CEC Protest

items.summary: The Quint fact-checked two viral videos claiming locals in Arunachal Pradesh chased out or fought China's People's Liberation Army. A reverse image search traced the first video to a Facebook post by a Nepali national promoting buffalo sacrifice during Dashain, while the second showed an Arunachal Pradesh police officer at a protest against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project dam. Sange Tenzin confirmed the uniformed personnel were from the state police.
items.title: Fact-check Debunks Viral Videos Claiming Locals Fight Chinese Troops in Arunachal Pradesh

items.summary: The Haryana government approved ₹340.78 crore for a new six-lane, 2.75 km-long elevated corridor at Sohna Chowk in Nuh district. The project addresses traffic congestion where National Highway 919 meets NH-248A by segregating through traffic between Gurugram and Nuh from local movements. It complements the existing operational Sohna Elevated Corridor, which opened in July 2022.
items.title: Haryana approves elevated corridor at Nuh highway junction

items.summary: State-owned oil companies raised commercial LPG prices by ₹10, bringing the rate to ₹2,820 per 19-kilogramme cylinder effective today. Aviation turbine fuel rose ₹1.37 per litre to ₹138.50. This marks the second consecutive monthly increase in commercial LPG and the fourth straight month of aviation fuel hikes, driven by firming international benchmarks. Prices are revised on the first day of each month and may vary across states due to local taxes.
items.title: State Oil Firms Raise Commercial LPG and Aviation Fuel Prices

items.summary: SJVN Limited reported standalone net profit of ₹736.73 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from ₹372.28 crore a year earlier, driven by higher revenues and regulatory tariff adjustments. Standalone revenue rose to ₹1,416.99 crore from ₹942.03 crore. The Board approved the unaudited results on October 30, 2026; auditors Charanjit Singh and Associates conducted a limited review.
items.title: SJVN Posts Higher Standalone Net Profit in Q2 FY27

items.summary: At an event in New York, Aman Singh, lead AI Engineer at Arca, described how the firm uses agents for long-horizon financial work while keeping humans in control. Arca raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock. Agents handle analysis and proposing solutions but cannot move money; trading stays with human advisors. Singh said safety restrictions are fully deterministic and take decision-making off the agent's hands. The firm uses models from Anthropic and OpenAI through its own harness, plus a memory system to track tasks across days. He summarized the approach as agents prompting people more than people prompt agents.
items.title: Arca Uses AI Agents That Prompt Human Advisors

items.summary: Adyant Alpha Power Private Limited, part of the Datta Infra Group, signed a 110 MW wind power purchase agreement with SJVN Limited for a project in Davanagere, Karnataka. The group said this pushes its cumulative signed agreements past 600 MW and adds to commissioned capacity of 50 MW plus more than 300 MW under construction.
items.title: Datta Infra Group Signs Wind PPA, Crosses 600 MW

items.summary: A newsletter episode titled EP231 explains several artificial intelligence concepts, including agentic AI, large reasoning models, vector databases, retrieval augmented generation, and the Model Context Protocol. It then reviews changes across six generations of OpenAI's GPT series from 2019 to 2026, noting parameter counts for earlier models and context window sizes for later ones. The episode also covers interview preparation topics and a high-level explanation of how GPUs work through parallel processing units.
items.title: Newsletter Explains AI Terms and GPT Generations

items.summary: Katoen Natie has put two all-electric mobile harbour cranes into service at the Port of Antwerp, with four more planned across three deep-sea multipurpose terminals. The completed fleet will include four 200-tonne cranes and two 150-tonne machines, reaching a paired lifting capacity of 400 tonnes. Katoen Natie expects them to displace as much as 500,000 litres of diesel annually once operating.
items.title: Katoen Natie Electrifies Antwerp Harbour Cranes

items.summary: Global Voices published an interview with Nazgul Aidabossynova, a local activist in the village of Qyzylsay, southern Kazakhstan. In 2026 she implemented a project under the Digital Spark granting scheme to help rural women improve their livelihoods through training on smartphones, eGov services, digital security, and documenting community problems such as water shortages. The initiative ran four practical sessions for ten participating women. Aidabossynova said the most valuable lesson is that digital literacy has the greatest impact when it is directly connected to people’s real, daily needs.
items.title: Kazakh women form collectives for water and digital rights
